purpose: A self-contained vRO test/demonstration workflow ("Switch Boolean Cases", category VMware.PSCoE) that exercises a system-generated switch item with three boolean cases. It reads the workflow-scope boolean attribute `isEnabled` and dispatches to one of three script tasks — true, false, or a catch-all default — each of which writes a single fixed line to the vRO system log via System.log, then converges on a normal (non-throwing) end. It has no inputs, no outputs, no external system calls, and no side effects beyond log lines; its entire observable behaviour is which of three log strings is emitted.

external_systems.how: Each of the three branch tasks calls System.log exactly once with a literal string. This is the only external interaction in the workflow; no plugin objects, no configuration elements, no actions, no linked or launched workflows.
items: System.log("Boolean value is undefined") — item4 / handleUndefined

decisions.item: item1 — switch item "switchByBoolean" (root_item, the entry point)
decisions.condition: Value of the workflow attribute `isEnabled` (boolean), bound in as `isEnabled`. The system-generated dispatch script is: if (isEnabled === true) return "item2"; else if (isEnabled === false) return "item3"; else if (true) return "item4". Note strict identity comparison — no truthiness coercion — and the third case is an unconditional default with an empty condition name (comparator 6), matching anything the first two do not, including null/undefined.

branches.does: Logs "Feature is enabled", then flows to item0.
Logs "Feature is disabled", then flows to item0.

branches.when: isEnabled is anything else — in practice null/undefined, since the attribute is declared with no value and nothing in this workflow ever assigns it
branches.does: Logs "Boolean value is undefined", then flows to item0.

decisions.condition: Reached unconditionally from whichever branch ran (item2, item3, or item4 all have out_name = item0).

branches.does: end_mode "0": the workflow finishes normally (success). It does NOT throw. There is no error-throwing end item anywhere in this workflow.

side_effects: Writes exactly one line to the vRO server log per execution — one of "Feature is enabled", "Feature is disabled", or "Boolean value is undefined". Exactly one branch runs; the three are mutually exclusive.
No state is mutated: the `isEnabled` attribute is read-only in practice (bound in to the switch via in_bindings, never written by any out_binding or script).
No files, no network calls, no other workflows started or invoked, no plugin/inventory objects touched, no secrets involved.
assumptions: `isEnabled` is a mutable workflow attribute (read_only: false) declared with value null and is_null_sentinel false — i.e. no value was configured at all, as opposed to an explicit __NULL__ sentinel. Nothing in this workflow assigns it, and there are no inputs, so on a plain run it is null/undefined and the default branch (item4) is the only one that actually executes. The true/false branches are reachable only if an external caller or test harness seeds the attribute before/at start.

The switch script is the authoritative dispatch logic; the numeric `comparator` codes (0 for the true case, 1 for the false case, 6 for the default) are the vRO encoding of that same script and should not be reimplemented independently. Treat comparator 6 with an empty condition name as "default", not as a comparison.

Comparison is strict (===). A truthy non-boolean value (e.g. the string "true", or 1) falls to the default branch, not to item2. A converted implementation must preserve this rather than using loose/truthy checks.

Execution order within the graph is deterministic and acyclic (depth 2, no cycles, all 5 items reachable, no unreachable items). There is no error handling: no item defines catch_name, so any runtime failure propagates as a workflow failure.

open_questions.question: How is `isEnabled` intended to be set? The workflow exposes no inputs and never assigns the attribute, so as written only the default branch is exercisable. Is the true/false behaviour meant to be driven by a test harness seeding the attribute, or was an input parameter intended and omitted?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the converted artifact should expose `isEnabled` as a parameter/argument (so all three branches are testable) or keep it as an internal, always-null variable where only the "undefined" path can ever run. Test authors need to know whether the true/false cases are legitimately reachable.

confidence_reason: The full item graph, the system-generated switch dispatch script, and all three branch scripts are present and self-contained. There are no actions (script_module), no linked or launched workflows, no plugin types, no configuration references, and no OGNL presentation logic — nothing behind an opaque boundary. The only residual uncertainty is intent around how `isEnabled` gets populated, which affects reachability of branches but not the specified behaviour of any branch.
